questionText:
Read the following excerpt on natural resource economics and answer the questions that follow:

In 1968, biologist Garrett Hardin published his famous essay 'The Tragedy of the Commons' in the journal Science. Hardin presented a scenario of an open-access pasture shared by independent herdsmen. Each rational herdsman seeks to maximize individual economic gain. When deciding whether to add another cow to the common pasture, the herdsman receives all the direct financial benefit (+1) from selling the animal. However, the negative impact of overgrazing caused by the additional cow is shared among all the herdsmen using the pasture, so the individual herdsman suffers only a fraction of the cost (-1/n). Consequently, every herdsman is locked into a system that compels him to expand his herd without limit—in a world that is finite. Ruin is the destination toward which all men rush, each pursuing his own best interest in a society that believes in the freedom of the commons. Hardin concluded that the only solutions to avert ecological catastrophe were either private property rights (privatization) or coercive governmental regulation ('mutual coercion, mutually agreed upon'). Decades later, political scientist Elinor Ostrom challenged this rigid dichotomy, proving that communities often self-govern common pool resources (CPRs) sustainably without either state coercion or privatization.

Question: How did Nobel laureate Elinor Ostrom fundamentally challenge Garrett Hardin's conclusions regarding common property resources?

options.text: She demonstrated that local resource users can self-organize robust community institutions to sustainably govern commons without private ownership or state control
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT principle for Elinor Ostrom Alternative Paradigm.

options.text: She proved that government agencies never make mistakes
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: She showed that animals never overgraze even when pasture grass is exhausted
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: She proved that natural resources on Earth are completely infinite and inexhaustible
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Environmental and Natural Resource Economics (Elinor Ostrom Alternative Paradigm):
She demonstrated that local resource users can self-organize robust community institutions to sustainably govern commons without private ownership or state control

Detailed Analysis:
Elinor Ostrom documented hundreds of enduring community-managed CPRs, showing that user self-governance successfully avoids resource depletion.
Hence, Option B is correct.

Therefore, option (A) is the correct answer.

topic: Elinor Ostrom Nobel Memorial Prize Contribution
questionText:
Match the resource concept in List I with its pioneer or economic definition in List II:

List I:
(A) The Tragedy of the Commons (1968)
(B) Governing the Commons (Nobel Prize 2009)
(C) Hubbert Peak Oil Theory (1956)
(D) Maximum Sustainable Yield (MSY)

List II:
(I) Garrett Hardin: open-access commons face inevitable ruin without private property or state coercion
(II) Elinor Ostrom: user communities can sustainably govern common pool resources through self-organized rules without state intervention
(III) M. King Hubbert: crude oil extraction follows a bell-shaped curve, peaking before irreversible terminal decline
(IV) The maximum harvest rate that can be extracted indefinitely from a renewable resource without depleting the base stock

questionText:
Arrange the clinical phases in an individual exposed to an acute, whole-body ionizing radiation dose (>4–6 Sieverts):
(I) Prodromal phase: rapid onset of nausea, severe vomiting, fatigue, and diarrhea within hours of exposure
(II) Latent phase: temporary apparent clinical improvement where symptoms subside for several days to weeks
(III) Manifest illness phase: massive collapse of hematopoietic bone marrow, extensive internal hemorrhaging, immune depletion, and intestinal lining sloughing
(IV) Death from opportunistic infections and septic shock unless rescued by bone marrow transplant
